How to set a hard spend limit on OpenAI and Anthropic API calls

Three layers catch three different failures. Use all three; none replaces the others.

LayerCatchesMisses
Provider console limit and alertsEverything, even when your code is wrong; it is the last lineWho or what spent it: one user or one agent run stops everyone; depending on the setting it may alert rather than refuse
Static checks before code ships (LLM Call Cost Scan)Calls with no output cap, calls inside loops, oversized models, before they runAnything that depends on real traffic
A guard in the request path (this tool)One user, feature, key or run crossing its own budget; loops; requests with no cap; unpriced modelsCalls that bypass it, which is why the provider limit stays on

Hold the worst case, then settle the real cost

A guard that counts spend after responses come back is too late under concurrency: twenty parallel calls all see the same remaining budget. LLM Spend Guard prices each call's worst case before it is sent: a deliberately high input estimate (bytes of the request divided by three) plus the full output cap. It holds that amount against every budget the call belongs to. The real cost from the response's usage then replaces the hold. A call that never reports back is charged at its hold, never at zero.

Budgets: scope × window

Each budget has a scope (global, user, feature, key, run), a window (UTC minute, hour, day, month, or total) and a dollar limit, a call limit or both. A per-run total call limit is a step cap for an agent. Calls with no user still count, in one shared (none) bucket, so anonymous traffic cannot slip past a per-user cap.

Breakers: stop the loop, not just the bill

A budget eventually stops a loop, but only after the loop has spent the budget. Breakers watch a rolling window and open early:

  • maxRepeats: the same request (same model and input) more than n times in repeatWindowSec. This catches an agent re-sending one failing tool call.
  • maxCallsPerMinute and maxSpendPerMinuteUsd: a burst far above normal.

An open breaker refuses calls in its scope for cooldownSec. The proxy answers 429 with Retry-After, so a well-behaved client waits instead of hammering.

Fail closed

By default a model with no configured price is refused (so a new model name cannot slip past every budget at $0), and a request with no output cap is refused. Set defaultMaxOutputTokens to add a cap instead, and maxOutputTokens to clamp any cap to a ceiling.

A policy to start from

{
  "mode": "observe",
  "prices": { "your-model-name": { "in": 0, "out": 0, "cacheRead": 0 } },
  "defaultMaxOutputTokens": 1024,
  "maxOutputTokens": 8192,
  "budgets": [
    { "id": "org-day",   "scope": "global", "window": "day",   "limitUsd": 25 },
    { "id": "org-month", "scope": "global", "window": "month", "limitUsd": 400 },
    { "id": "user-day",  "scope": "user",   "window": "day",   "limitUsd": 2 },
    { "id": "run-total", "scope": "run",    "window": "total", "limitUsd": 3, "limitCalls": 150 }
  ],
  "breakers": [
    { "id": "loop",  "scope": "run",    "maxRepeats": 20, "repeatWindowSec": 300, "cooldownSec": 900 },
    { "id": "burst", "scope": "global", "maxCallsPerMinute": 120, "cooldownSec": 120 }
  ]
}

Fill in your models' current per-million-token prices from your provider's pricing page; the zeros above are placeholders, not rates. Run it in observe mode first: it logs every call it would refuse and refuses none. Replay last month's log through it on the simulator, adjust, then set "mode": "enforce".

Other tools that do some of this

Gateways and observability platforms such as LiteLLM, Portkey and Helicone offer budgets, rate limits or spend dashboards in various forms; check their current documentation for what each enforces and on which plan. Use this tool if you want a dependency-free file you can read in an hour. It holds worst-case cost before a call, breaks on repeated requests per agent run, refuses unpriced models by default, and replays a log offline. Questions

Is the provider's own spend limit enough?

Keep it on: it is the backstop that works even when your code is wrong. But it sees the whole organisation or project, not one user, feature or agent run, and depending on the provider and setting it may alert rather than refuse, or act after usage is counted. A guard in your own path can refuse one runaway user or run while everyone else keeps working.

Why reserve the worst case before a call?

Counting spend after responses arrive lets every concurrent call see the same remaining budget, so twenty parallel calls can all start under a limit that only one of them fits. Holding each call's worst case (input estimate plus full output cap) first means the budget is never promised twice.

What should a first policy look like?

A global daily and monthly dollar cap, a smaller per-user daily cap, a per-run total and step cap for agents, an output-token ceiling, a repeat breaker per run, and a calls-per-minute breaker globally. Start it in observe mode for a week, read what it would have refused, then switch to enforce.

Would a spend cap have stopped your runaway LLM bill?

An agent stuck retrying one tool call, a loop with no exit, a prompt that asks for the full output limit: each can spend a month of OpenAI or Anthropic budget in an afternoon. LLM Spend Guard sits in front of your calls and refuses one before it is sent when it would cross a hard dollar budget per user, feature, API key or agent run, or when a loop breaker sees the same request again and again.

Replay your own usage log through a policy below to see what it would have refused. Then run the same policy as a local proxy (one base-URL change) or as a library call around your SDK.

The simulator runs in this browser. Your log and policy never leave your device.

1. Replay a usage log through a policy

Rows need a model and token counts in Anthropic (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) or OpenAI (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) form, nested under usage or flat. Optional: created_at, user, feature, run_id/trace_id, and prompt_hash (without it a replay cannot see repeats). Prices come from the policy: put in your provider's current rates.

2. What the policy would have done

3. Enforce it: proxy or library

Proxy (Node 18+, no dependencies). Change the SDK's base URL and every call passes the guard:

node cli.mjs init guard-policy.json        # then put in your models and current prices
node cli.mjs check-policy guard-policy.json  # summary + gaps (no global cap? no breakers?)
node cli.mjs proxy guard-policy.json --port 8787

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/anthropic
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/openai/v1
# optional headers per request: x-guard-user, x-guard-feature, x-guard-run

A refused call gets the provider's own error shape: HTTP 402 when a budget is spent (SDKs do not retry it) and 429 with Retry-After while a breaker is open. Streams are passed through byte for byte and settled from the usage they report.

Library, around any SDK call:

import { createGuard } from './guard.mjs';
const guard = createGuard(policy, { onEvent: (e) => e.type === 'alert' && notify(e) });

const text = await guard.guarded(
  { model, maxOutputTokens: 1024, input: messages, scope: { user: userId, run: runId } },
  async (d) => {
    const r = await client.messages.create({ model, max_tokens: d.maxOutputTokens, messages });
    return { result: r, usage: { input: r.usage.input_tokens, output: r.usage.output_tokens } };
  });

Read how to set a hard spend limit on OpenAI and Anthropic API calls for what each control catches and where provider-side limits still matter.

Questions

How do I put a hard limit on my OpenAI or Anthropic API spend?

Set the provider's own organisation or project limit as the backstop, then put a guard in front of your calls that refuses a request before it is sent when it would cross a budget. LLM Spend Guard does that as a local proxy (change the SDK base URL) or as a library call around your SDK call, with budgets per user, feature, key and agent run.

How does it stop concurrent calls overshooting a budget?

Each call holds its worst-case cost (a high estimate of its input plus its full output cap) against every budget before it is sent, like a card hold. Concurrent calls cannot all fit into the same remaining dollar. When the response reports real usage, the actual cost replaces the hold.

What is a runaway loop breaker?

An agent that keeps retrying the same tool call, or a bug that calls the model in a tight loop, can spend a month's budget in minutes. A breaker watches a rolling window and opens when one run sends the same request too many times, or calls or spend per minute pass a limit; while open it refuses calls for a cooldown, and the proxy answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

Is my usage log uploaded?

No. The simulator on this page replays the log you paste in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The proxy runs on your machine or your server, and only talks to the provider you point it at.
